Con los naturales se cuenta y se reparte: With the naturals you count and share out in whole parts, and the previous topic taught you to break them into primes. Now we share out what does not fit into whole parts, and for that new numbers are needed. The gcd and the lcm you have just learned are the two tools this topic uses non-stop: one to simplify, the other to add.
Con los naturales no se puede repartir u: With the naturals you cannot share a pizza among three. A new number is needed: the fraction. The bottom one (denominator) says how many equal parts the unit is divided into; the top one (numerator), how many of those parts we take.
Una fracción es además, y esto es lo que: A fraction is also, and this is what makes it powerful, three things at once: a part of a whole, an unfinished division ($3:4$) and a particular point on the number line ($0{.}75$).
Los egipcios, hace 4000 años, solo admit: The Egyptians, 4000 years ago, only admitted fractions with numerator 1 (called unit fractions): to write $\frac{3}{4}$ they put $\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{4}$. The Rhind papyrus is basically a table for converting fractions into that form. Our way of writing them, with the bar in the middle, comes from the Arab mathematicians of the twelfth century.

Una pantalla 16:9 y otra de 1920×1080 ti: A 16:9 screen and a 1920×1080 one have the same shape because $\frac{1920}{1080}$ simplifies to $\frac{16}{9}$. All web page layout, photo cropping and cinema formats speak in equivalent fractions, and the black bars on a film shown on television are exactly the price of mixing two fractions that are not.

La música occidental es aritmética de fr: Western music is fraction arithmetic. Two notes sound well together when their frequencies are in a simple ratio: $2/1$ is the octave, $3/2$ the fifth, $4/3$ the fourth. Pythagoras built a whole scale by chaining fifths, and ran into the fact that twelve fifths do not land exactly on seven octaves —$(3/2)^{12}$ is not $2^7$—; that mismatch, the Pythagorean comma, is why pianos are tuned with a small fudge on every note.
